bug_semantics: Apache Airflow Task SDK deserialized JSON Variables and then dispatched masking on the top-level Python type. After json.loads, only str values (and, after CVE-2026-59244, dict values) were passed to mask_secret; a top-level list matched neither branch and was returned unmasked. Secrets stored as a JSON array therefore never entered the secrets masker, so they appeared in cleartext in task logs and in the Rendered Templates UI to any authenticated user who could read those views. add_mask already walked iterables under a supplied name, so nested lists inside a dict were masked; only a top-level list was skipped. The correct list handling is mask_secret(list, variable_key) so elements inherit the Variable key's sensitivity without anonymously over-masking ordinary values.
flaw_origin: The list omission was first written in apache/airflow#50895 member 12b6fa60256e8a8f896e6ac338a01d63e7ca8469 (Amogh Desai, 2025-05-22). The previous member 2ecd61b9b4ddabadf723016d3768b6db240ddbbe called mask_secret(var_val, key) unconditionally after deserialize, which would have walked lists under the Variable key (the same rule the 2026 fix restored). 12b6fa6 replaced that call with `if isinstance(var_val, str): mask_secret(var_val, key)` in _get_variable, so lists and dicts fell through unmasked. GitHub squash-merged those two members as 98f918150e717777088c884f6ee275d1912f9209 on main. Later 049123e8c730ea471dc5e93b69a21d6b1fddba91 copied the str-only gate onto the SecretCache path, and cd28fbde0bef19837d2e85d1de256c7bc1d7d370 (CVE-2026-59244 / #68975) refactored it into _mask_and_deserialize_variable and added a dict branch while still skipping lists; those are carriers/incomplete sibling fixes, not the first write.
